deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a damping (logarithmic decrement) series from the Gauss–Weber magnetometer and induction experiments. 'Kette offen/geschlossen' means the circuit (multiplier coil) is open or closed. The swing period is about 42.4 s. My check: 51 swings from 11h21'18.25" to 11h57'18.7" give 2160.45 s, i.e. 42.36 s per swing. Likewise 17 swings from 102 to 119 take 720.2 s.

(1) Columns. Each row gives the swing number n, occasionally a clock time, a scale reading near 978, an amplitude A_n, and log10 A_n to 5 places. Example: log10(399.8) = 2.60184. The meaning of the ~978 column is my guess: it is probably a turning-point or rest-point reading, but this is uncertain.

(2) Group means. For swings 102–106, the mean of the five logs is (2.60184+2.60043+2.59879+2.59627+2.59390)/5 = 2.598246. Gauss writes this as '2.59824.6'; it belongs to the middle swing, 104. For swings 119–123, the mean is (2.55334+2.55060+2.54827+2.54642+2.54370)/5 = 2.548466 ('2.54846.6'), belonging to swing 121.

(3) Logarithmic decrement per swing. D.L. = (2.598246 − 2.548466)/(121−104) = 0.049780/17 = 0.0029282. Gauss records it in units of 1e-5 as 'D.L 292.82' (open circuit), attached to midpoint 112½.

The same procedure on the previous page gives three more values:
- Open circuit, swings 53 and 71: (2.854880 − 2.813368)/18 = 230.62e-5, at midpoint 62.
- Closed circuit, swings 79 and 96: (2.767750 − 2.635294)/17 = 779.15e-5, at midpoint 87½.
- Open, at 11½ (218.09) and closed, at 36½ (761.46): these come from earlier sheets.

(4) Recapitulation. The open and closed decrements alternate in time. To compare them at the same epoch, Gauss linearly interpolates the other state (pencil, 'interpolirt'):
- At 36½: open = 218.09 + (25/50.5)(230.62−218.09) = 224.29. Difference: 761.46 − 224.29 = 537.17.
- At 62: closed = (761.46+779.15)/2 = 770.30 (exact 770.305). Difference: 770.30 − 230.62 = 539.68.
- At 87½: open = 230.62 + (25.5/50.5)(292.82−230.62) = 262.03. Difference: 779.15 − 262.03 = 517.12.

The final 538,42 equals (537.17+539.68)/2 = 538.425. So the third, discordant value 517.12 (marked with a sign) was apparently excluded. The mean of all three would be 531.32.

Result: the part of the logarithmic decrement caused by the induced currents in the closed circuit is about 538.4e-5 per swing (log10 units). This is a drift-corrected 'closed minus open' damping. Temperature 8.0 °C.
errors: No arithmetic errors found. All logarithms, the group means 2.598246 and 2.548466, the decrement 292.82, and the interpolations 224.29, 770.30, 262.03 and the differences check to the last digit (770.305 rounded to 770.30).

Methodological point, not an error: 538.42 is the mean of only the first two differences. The third (517.12) is silently dropped, presumably because the open-circuit damping rose sharply (230.62 to 292.82), which makes linear interpolation doubtful.

results.what: Logarithmic decrement from the difference of means of log amplitudes of two groups of 5 swings, divided by the swing separation
results.modern_name: logarithmic decrement of a damped oscillator (group-averaged estimate)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and W. Weber, Göttingen magnetic observations, 1830s (standard practice)

results.what: Separation of the induction (electromagnetic) damping from air/other damping by alternating open/closed circuit and linearly interpolating to common epochs
results.modern_name: electromagnetic (eddy/induction-current) damping measurement with drift correction
results.usually_credited_to: Wilhelm Weber (with Gauss), late 1830s, e.g. in 'Resultate aus den Beobachtungen des magnetischen Vereins'

deep.surprise_reason: Routine experimental data reduction from the well-documented Gauss–Weber induction and damping experiments; no new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: = 538.425, the final 538,42 (mean of first two differences only)

transcription_corrections: Left-margin '62' and '.15' are cut-off fragments of the facing page (verso/previous sheet), not part of this page's content.
'D.L 292.82' belongs to the bracketed pair 102–106 / 119–123, not to a row numbered 62.
The columns 'interpolirt' (224.29, 770.30, 262.03), the differences 537.17, 539.68, 517.12 and the result 538,42 are in pencil, a later addition. A small mark follows 517.12.
Faint pencil numbers near the bottom (approximately '6138' and '1253') are omitted in the machine transcription; they are archival or unrelated.
Previous-page transcription error, for context: rows 94–98 repeat the ~978 value in the amplitude column. The amplitudes must be about 447.7, 439.4, 431.8, 424.2, 416.4 to give the stated logs.
